sections.html:
Deed and official records for Leon County are online. The County Clerk's office in Centerville also has eight public search stations, and staff will show you how the indexes work, though you are welcome to do your own research.

The office is on the first floor at 155 North Cass Street, Centerville, TX 75833. A few house rules apply:

  • No photographs of the large Tobin maps or of images on the public stations, and no flash photography.
  • Carrying a document, page or volume out of the office is a state jail felony (Penal Code 32.47).
  • Staff give no legal advice, do not decide who owns surface or mineral rights, and do not run lien searches.
  • The clerk has no duty to search the records and vouch for what is or is not there.

sections.h2: Office hours, filing cutoff and fees
sections.html:
The office is open 7:45 a.m. to 4:45 p.m. every weekday with no lunch closure, but recording itself ends at 4 p.m. Anything that arrives later goes into the next business day's work. Cash, checks and major credit cards are accepted.

The posted charge is $15 for page one of an instrument and $4 for each page after it, on a schedule that began January 1, 2024. Electronic filing into the official records runs through three vendors: Simplifile, CSC and ePN. Fees shift over time, so confirm the amount with the clerk's staff before you pay.

Different deputies take different work. The chief deputy handles general recording, indexing and copy requests, while probate, civil filings, marriage licenses and vital records each have their own staff member and phone menu option. Say at the start of a call that you are asking about recording a deed. Clerks are not attorneys and cannot tell you what needs to be filed.

sections.h2: What Texas requires before a deed is recorded
sections.html:
A land conveyance can be recorded only after the owner signs it and either swears to it or acknowledges it, before two witnesses or before an officer such as a notary, county clerk, district clerk or county court judge (Property Code 12.001(b)).

Deed records take general and special warranty deeds, quitclaims, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds and tax deeds, plus lien releases, affidavits and contracts of sale. The statutory base is $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for later pages, with other clerk charges added, and a missing grantee mailing address can add $25. For a real filing, use the figure Leon County posts.

An old deed cannot be rewritten to add heirs. After an owner's death, an administered estate uses an executor's or administrator's deed, a muniment of title pairs a court order with the will, and an affidavit of heirship is the fallback when nothing else is available.

Leon County is rural, on Interstate 45 between Dallas and Houston. It has 16,894 residents, up 7.2 percent since 2020, and 9,255 housing units. Owners occupy 76.6 percent of homes, and the middle owned-home value is $186,400. Monthly housing costs run $1,557 for owners with a mortgage, $502 for owners without one, and $907 for renters. About 27.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, which matters for estates, since a parent's name often stays on the deed for years.

sections.h2: Who handles values and tax bills
sections.html:
The Leon Central Appraisal District sets values, and the county tax assessor-collector issues bills. For an account change or a value question, go to the appraisal district at 141 W. St. Mary's, Centerville, TX 75833, telephone 903-536-2252.

Collection firms chase delinquent accounts for each taxing unit. One Waco firm covers the county, a Corsicana firm covers Normangee ISD, and a Tyler firm covers Buffalo ISD, the City of Marquez and Oakwood ISD. If a collection letter shows up, the unit that sent it tells you which firm to contact.

Across Texas, values are set as of January 1, bills arrive in October, and penalty-free payment ends January 31. A tax lien takes hold every January 1, so a Leon County house enters any sale still owing that year's tax. Our Leon County property tax guide covers the tax office itself.

A protest of value goes to the review board in writing, due on the later of May 15 and the 30th day after the notice is delivered.

sections.h2: Title problems in the Leon County records
sections.html:
The commonest one is an estate nobody opened. Where 27.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, a parent's name often remains the last owner of record, and the file then needs a legal path to the heirs.

  • Four years from the date of death is the usual window to probate a will, and a judge may accept a late filing for an acceptable reason.
  • A small estate affidavit needs no will, no pending administration, assets up to $75,000 apart from homestead and exempt property, and every heir's agreement. Two disinterested witnesses swear to it, and the death must be at least 30 days old.
  • A muniment of title lets a will serve as proof of ownership when the only debts are real estate liens.
  • Heirs can file a sworn heirship statement with the Leon County Clerk, though nothing obliges a buyer or lender to rely on it.

Heirs who want a homestead exemption without being named on a recorded deed give the appraisal district a sworn statement of their interest, a death certificate and a current utility bill.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Leon County house with a title or lien problem?
sections.html:
Yes. A cash buyer can take the house exactly as it is, with the closing agent settling recorded items wherever a payoff is documented. If you found an unreleased mortgage, a probate gap or a back tax bill in the Leon County records, send us the details and we will outline the likely route to closing.

To make that first conversation useful, have the owner names, the date of any death, the lender on any old loan and your latest tax statement in front of you. The closing agent will use those to line up releases, payoffs and any estate paperwork before the day funds move.

faqs.q: What is the last hour to file a document in Leon County?
faqs.a: Recording ends at 4 p.m., although the office stays open until 4:45 p.m. on weekdays. Papers that arrive later are handled the following business day.

faqs.q: What fee applies to filing a deed with the Leon County Clerk?
faqs.a: The clerk lists $15 for page one and $4 for every added page of an instrument, effective January 1, 2024. Ask the office to confirm the amount when you file.

faqs.q: Are Leon County deed records available online?
faqs.a: Yes. Deed and official records are online, and the same records back to 1828 can be viewed on public stations in the Centerville office.

faqs.q: Will the Leon County Clerk tell me who owns the minerals?
faqs.a: No. Staff cannot determine surface or mineral ownership or run lien searches, so that work falls to a closing agent or a lawyer.

faqs.q: Where do I contest a Leon County appraisal?
faqs.a: Call the Leon Central Appraisal District at 903-536-2252. Written protests to the review board are due on the later of May 15 and the 30th day after delivery of the value notice.
